title: Juz' 'Amma, the shape
hook: thirty-seven surahs: the Day, the orphan, the soul, the One

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of An-Naba': the Day of fasl, when what was mixed is separated. Your line was the day of sorting.

Near the top of a hike, there's a moment when you turn around. The path you climbed is laid out below you, and for the first time you can see its shape: where it switched back, where it got steep, where you stopped for water. Since day one hundred fifty-nine, this path has walked backward through the last part of the Qur'an, from An-Nas on its final page to An-Naba' at the front. Yesterday it reached the start. So today, no new surah. Just a turn around, to look at the whole thing: thirty-seven surahs, and four things they keep coming back to.
screen: `TURNING AROUND NEAR THE TOP.` → `FROM AN-NAS BACK TO AN-NABA'.` → `THE WHOLE PATH IN VIEW.`

segments.voice: Juz' means a part. The Qur'an's surahs are of very different lengths, so later Muslims divided the text into thirty parts of roughly equal length, to be read in a month, a part a day, as some do in Ramadan. The division is a reading aid, not part of the revelation itself. The thirtieth part runs from Surah seventy-eight to the end, thirty-seven surahs, named for its first word, 'amma, about what. They're short, they rhyme, and several open with oaths: by the dawn, by the sun, by the fig and the olive. Under all that sound, four themes keep returning. The Day: An-Naba', Az-Zalzalah, Al-Qari'ah, the sorting and the weighing. The orphan: again and again the surahs ask who fed the orphan and who pushed him away, from Ad-Duha to Al-Ma'un. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came from an orphan's childhood himself, which gives those verses a sound all their own. The soul: Ash-Shams swears by the soul and the One who shaped it, and says whoever purifies it has succeeded. And the One: Al-Ikhlas, four short lines on the oneness of Allah. It's often the first part children learn by heart: short enough to hold, one surah at a time, and full of those four things.
screen: `JUZ' — ONE OF THIRTY PARTS.` · `THIRTY-SEVEN SHORT SURAHS.` · `THE DAY, THE ORPHAN, THE SOUL, THE ONE.` · `OFTEN LEARNED FIRST, BY HEART.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE JUZ'.`

segments.voice: Let the last few weeks come back one surah at a time: the whisperer that withdraws, daybreak, Say, He is Allah, the One, the morning light of Ad-Duha, the man who frowned, the trumpet and the crowds. Don't try to remember them all; notice which ones come back on their own. Hold three of their names, and ask what each one gave you.
Juz' 'Amma. The thirtieth part of the Qur'an, thirty-seven surahs named for their first word: the Day, the orphan, the soul, the One. Today's word.
Your line: the whole juz'. From An-Nas back to An-Naba', the path is in view. Day two hundred twenty-two, done.

howItsDone: Muslim children often learn Juz' 'Amma first, starting from its end (An-Nas) and working backward, and its short surahs are commonly recited in the daily prayers; the thirty-part division lets a reader finish the whole Qur'an across a month, as some do in Ramadan.
